safety_lead_time.comparison_action: decrease from SAP 4.0 days to 2.64 days

narrative: Material PL2__M790A183 shows variable daily demand (CV=0.62) with a statistically significant declining trend and moderately variable lead times (mean 5.4 days, CV=0.30). The current SAP policy holds zero safety stock, creating substantial stockout exposure at the 95% service level target. The recommended (r,Q) policy introduces a 2,128-unit safety buffer and consolidates replenishments to ~23 orders/year, reducing total annual inventory costs by approximately 30% while respecting the hard storage cap of 8,761 units.
warnings: Storage utilization at 100.0% — capacity constraint is binding; true EOQ (10,370) exceeds available space after safety stock allocation.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review reorder-point with fixed order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is mostly continuous (92.7% non-zero days) with a variable but not intermittent pattern (CV=0.62). The (r,Q) policy is optimal here as it directly addresses service level via safety stock dimensioning and minimizes total cost via EOQ. A periodic review policy would be less responsive given the lead-time variability observed.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 8,761 units is fully consumed by SS+OQ=8,761. Any demand spike requiring a larger buffer or MOQ rounding could breach capacity. Recommend reviewing warehouse allocation or negotiating a modest capacity increase to restore operating headroom.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (3,021) + Safety Stock (2,128) = 5,149 which is below max_storage_units (8,761); policy is feasible
